Compliance-Related Security Requirements

Introduction

Compliance requirements refer to the laws, regulations, and platform specifications that must be strictly followed during the development and operation of mini-programs and other businesses. These requirements stem not only from national-level laws and regulations (such as the Cybersecurity Law, Personal Information Protection Law, and Data Security Law) but also include access specifications of third-party platforms such as data platforms. These requirements are mandatory and must not be violated; otherwise, serious consequences such as legal risks, platform bans, and business removal may occur.

Data Security

Specifications based primarily on the data security laws and regulations of the business location. Details can be obtained through the public disclosure of cybersecurity information in the business location. For mini-program front-end developers, it is imperative to disable data desensitization, encrypted data transmission, etc.

Privacy Compliance

Based primarily on the personal data protection laws and regulations of the business location. Details can be obtained through the public disclosure of cybersecurity information in the business location. For mini-program developers, it is required to minimize the application for necessary personal information; display privacy agreements and policies on the page when releasing after passing the review; when using the mini-program, if user data collection is involved, an authorization pop-up must be displayed to obtain the user's authorization, and data collection can only be carried out after obtaining the user's explicit consent.

Content Security and Ecological Security

In the development and operation of mini-programs, the compliance of page content is a mandatory requirement of the platform and the laws and regulations of the country where the business is located. As a public-facing display platform, the content of mini-programs must strictly abide by national laws and regulations regarding politics, religion, terrorism, pornography, violence, prohibited and restricted products, etc. Mini-programs have a content inspection mechanism and violation penalty rules. Once non-compliant content is found, the mini-program may be removed, have its functions restricted, or have its account banned.

Key Points to Focus On

For developers, it is recommended to pay attention to the following key points.

Compliant Acquisition of Information

  • Privacy clauses must not be pre-checked by default.
  • Package authorization is prohibited; authorization should be applied for on demand and minimized.
  • Inducing users to provide information collection is prohibited, as is forcing/repeatedly pushing authorization pop-ups to users.
  • If the user does not agree to the authorization, they must not be forced to exit; content and services that can be used without authorization should be provided.
  • To obtain personal information of minors under the age of 14, the consent of the minor's parents or other guardians must be obtained.

Proper Handling of Authorized Data

  • Authorized data should be transmitted to the server using secure methods.
  • The use of authorized data must not exceed the scope agreed upon by the user.
  • When the service is terminated and the user explicitly requests data deletion, the data should be deleted in a timely and permanent manner. Except for data that is required to be retained in compliance with regulations within a fixed period.
  • In the event of a data breach, emergency measures should be taken promptly to prevent the continuous leakage of user data or the expansion of the impact. At the same time, report the handling situation to the Mini-Program Platform, regulatory authorities, and notify users to prevent infringements and attacks caused by data leakage.

Reasonable Domain Name Configuration

  • There is a domain name configuration entry in the mini-program management console. The scope of domain names allowed to be loaded by the mini-program should be reasonably designed to protect the security of the mini-program itself.
  • In the H5 domain name configuration of the web-view component, only configure trusted domain names to avoid illegal and non-compliant content placed by black and gray industries.
